title: The Straits Crisis
role: Advise the President of Republic A

rounds.event: Power B announces customs inspections around Island C and begins turning away selected commercial vessels. Ally D supports monitoring but is reluctant to authorize offensive operations from its territory. Ally E fears simultaneous escalation by a neighboring adversary. Intelligence assesses a 55% chance Power B intends a temporary coercive quarantine rather than an invasion.

choices.text: Begin Republic A-led naval escorts immediately without waiting for allied commitments.
Build a joint monitoring coalition, request Ally D ISR access, and set a 48-hour deadline before considering escorts.
Limit the response to sanctions and public condemnation.

rounds.event: Ally D privately agrees to expanded ISR but warns that unilateral strikes by Republic A would trigger a cabinet crisis. Ally E offers logistics support if Republic A forces remain available for its regional contingencies.

choices.text: Accept differentiated allied roles and publicly frame the coalition as unified around a common objective.
Demand identical military commitments from Allies D and E to demonstrate resolve.
Prepare a unilateral operation and keep allied consultations minimal.

rounds.event: New intelligence lowers the assessed invasion risk to 25%. Power B offers to lift inspections if Island C delays a planned sovereignty-related referendum. Island C rejects the condition.

choices.text: Shift toward negotiated de-escalation while maintaining monitoring and a reversible escort option.
Maintain the original escalation plan because changing course would damage credibility.
Publicly pressure Island C to accept Power B's condition to end the crisis.

rounds.event: A Power B coast guard vessel collides with a ship chartered by Ally F carrying Island C cargo. No deaths occur. Power B calls it an accident and offers talks.

choices.text: Convene emergency allied talks, demand safety guarantees, and postpone irreversible military action for 24 hours.
Treat the collision as deliberate aggression and begin armed escorts immediately.
Avoid involvement and leave Island C and Power B to negotiate bilaterally.

title: The Lithography Coalition
role: Advise Republic A's National Security Advisor

rounds.event: Republic A asks Allies B and C to tighten controls on advanced industrial equipment exports to Power D. A narrow package may delay a strategic capability by 12 to 18 months; a maximal package promises greater delay but carries high allied noncompliance risk.

choices.text: Demand the maximal package immediately and threaten secondary restrictions on allied firms that do not comply.
Negotiate a narrower common floor, pair it with adjustment support, and establish a joint review mechanism.
Delay controls until every ally voluntarily agrees to Republic A's position.

rounds.event: A major supplier in Ally B warns that extraterritorial controls could push R&D outside Republic A-linked supply chains. Ally C requests a two-year review clause.

choices.text: Accept a review clause and define measurable security triggers for renewal.
Reject any review clause and insist that security requires permanent restrictions.
Exempt both allies and rely only on Republic A's controls.

rounds.event: New technical analysis finds the targeted bottleneck in Power D is less severe than first estimated, reducing the expected security benefit of the broadest controls.

choices.text: Narrow the package and explain the change as an evidence-based adjustment.
Keep the maximal package to avoid signaling weakness.
Abandon the control effort entirely.

rounds.event: Power D restricts exports of a specialty material used by allied manufacturers but quietly signals willingness to reverse the measure if the coalition avoids further expansion.

choices.text: Coordinate stockpiles and diversification with allies while opening a channel to test Power D's offer.
Immediately expand controls into additional sectors in retaliation.
Unilaterally suspend the controls to restore material access.
